notes: Grounded against duel.tsx, duel-board.tsx, screens.tsx, shop-os.tsx, icons.tsx, wm.tsx/wm.css and styles.css as they stand today (kp-dive2 dock, not the older kp-duel-* block, which is dead CSS from an earlier layout). Two load-bearing discoveries: (1) styles.css already carries unwired scaffolding for exactly this pass: .kp-pieces/.kp-piece-slot/.kp-piece-preview/.kp-pp-bg/.kp-pp-hi/.kp-pp-arm/.kp-pp-node (44px piece glyph, lines ~1548-1611) and .kp-dghost/.kp-dghost-arm/.kp-dghost-node (board hover ghost, lines ~1766-1780, already CSS-wired to :hover) plus .kp-dblock-patchable (gold pulse ring on legal slag, line ~3330). Every spec below reuses these rather than inventing parallel chrome. (2) DuelBoard's local armLines(mask, className, width) helper (duel-board.tsx:16-34) is the only arm-mask renderer in the codebase; every item below that needs a piece glyph asks for it to be generalized into one shared component rather than reimplemented per surface. Zero art ordered for piece glyphs (SVG-first, per brief); one art order filed for the DARKNET.LNK icon, which is a deliberate exception (see darknet-window spec) to the desktop's all-vector-rect icon idiom. Credit-adjacency (tutorial/ledger.md 'night-shop-credit-adjacency', screens.tsx:618-633) is applied to every new spend row here: DARKNET buy, boost bay install. Anchor note for tutorial-agent: no new kp-teach-<anchor> CSS needed this pass. The retiring dock PATCH CELL button already anchors kp-teach-patch, and the new pouch strip sits in the exact same dock slot, so that anchor still points correctly. DARKNET and boost-bay first-sight moments should reuse the existing kp-teach-screen (bottom-center overlay) anchor, proven for whole-window/whole-card introductions elsewhere. Inline copy in the specs below is placeholder for layout sizing only; narrative-director owns final wording, no em or en dashes even in these placeholders. This file replaces the prior cycle's ux-agent.json (brief teaching-2026-07-26), whose items have already shipped per the repo's git history.

items.spec:
Replace the count-only PATCH CELL button with a glyph-based pouch across three surfaces, all reading from the same ordered list of up to 5 held pieces (each an arm mask plus a fixed rotation rolled at acquisition, never rotated in hand). First, extract DuelBoard's local armLines(mask, className, width) into a small shared PieceGlyph({ mask, size, tone }) component (tone selects a stroke/fill class set: 'signal' default, 'gold' armed, 'dim' empty/locked, 'crimson' illegal) so every surface below draws the same shapes at different sizes instead of six bespoke renderers. Reuse the existing .kp-pp-bg/.kp-pp-arm/.kp-pp-node classes (styles.css ~1569-1587) as the base stroke set; PieceGlyph just parameterizes the box size instead of the hardcoded 44px .kp-piece-preview.

SURFACE 1: duel dock (kp-dive2-dock, duel.tsx footer ~707-800). The pouch occupies the exact dock slot the current PATCH CELL button uses (a 4th item inside kp-dock-abilities, alongside SCAN/ATTACK/DEFEND), not a new dock row. Wrap it in the existing .kp-ability shell (same padding/border/background as the program buttons, min-width 118px) so overall dock rhythm is unchanged, but its interior is a new .kp-pouch-row: flex, wrap, gap 4px, max-width 108px, holding up to 5 .kp-pouch-slot glyph buttons at 24x24px each (so 4 fit per row, the 5th always wraps to a second internal row rather than growing the dock item wider). Arm stroke-width at this size is 3px (matches the board's stroke-width 6 at 48px cells, same ~12.5% ratio) so all four shapes (2 opposite arms / 2 adjacent arms / 3 arms / 4 arms) stay visually distinct at dock scale. Label above the row stays 'PATCH' at the same 10px dim caps style as the RAM/ability labels.

SURFACE 2: night screen (UpgradeScreen, screens.tsx ~618-662). The old kp-cellrow BUY PATCH CELL button is retired (acquisition moves to DARKNET.LNK, see darknet-window). What remains in its slot is a read-only status line: a small (28px) pouch strip using the same PieceGlyph component, plus '.kp-rail-dim' text 'buy pieces at DARKNET.LNK' (placeholder). This keeps the credits-adjacent informational habit UpgradeScreen already has (STRAIN/credits/rest all on one line) without offering an action that no longer exists here.

SURFACE 3: kit card (KitScreen's kp-kit-cells card, screens.tsx ~319-335). This is the full-fidelity display: exactly 5 labeled slots at 44px using the pre-existing .kp-piece-slot/.kp-piece-preview scaffolding verbatim (no new CSS needed here beyond wiring PieceGlyph into it), each captioned with its shape name (STRAIGHT/ELBOW/TEE/CROSS placeholder caps) when holding, or a dashed dim placeholder box when empty. This card is also where patch-craft-flow's interactive states layer on top (see that item).

Four states apply wherever a pouch renders: EMPTY (dashed 1px dim outline box, no glyph, non-interactive), HOLDING (solid line-colored box, signal-tone glyph, clickable), ARMED-FOR-PLACEMENT (dock/craft only: gold outline + glow, reuse the exact .kp-ability-arming border-color/box-shadow values already defined, applied to the single selected .kp-pouch-slot), USED-THIS-TURN (dock only: once the per-turn placement budget is spent, the whole pouch dock item takes the existing .kp-prog-offline treatment (opacity .35, saturate .3), identical to how SCAN/ATTACK/DEFEND already go offline when used or locked; individual pieces remain visible through the dim, communicating 'still held, not spendable this turn'). Selecting a different held piece while one is armed swaps the arm target immediately (same 'any program press abandons the prior aim' rule already applied to SCAN/ATTACK/DEFEND in duel.tsx onProgram), no extra confirm. Selecting the same armed piece again, or ESC, cancels back to HOLDING (reuse the existing setPlacing(false)/ESC handler path).
acceptance: at 5/5 held pieces, the dock pouch item's own rendered width never exceeds 120px (matching the existing .kp-ability min-width of 118px); glyphs wrap to two internal rows (4 then 1) instead of the item growing wider

on a 360px wide viewport, RAM readout + SCAN + ATTACK + DEFEND + POUCH + END TURN require no horizontal scroll; kp-dock-abilities' existing flex-wrap already reflows its 4 items before any is clipped, and if the pouch wraps to two internal rows the whole kp-dive2-dock bar simply grows taller (align-items: center keeps END TURN vertically centered, never cut off)

the armed piece's 4-bit arm mask (2 opposite, 2 adjacent, 3, or 4 arms) is visually distinguishable from the other three shapes at the dock's 24x24px glyph box with 3px arm stroke, including while the screen is mid kp-shake-3 (the shake class lives on the kp-dive2 root, so the whole dock moves, not just the board; legibility must not depend on the dock holding still)
clicking a held dock slot arms it (gold outline) and opens the existing target-bar pattern; clicking it again or pressing ESC returns it to HOLDING with no side effects
once econ.placedThisTurn (or its renamed equivalent) is true, every glyph in the dock pouch is still visible through the dim, not hidden

the UpgradeScreen pouch status line and the KitScreen kit card both read the identical pouch data as the dock, so a piece placed mid dive and one bought at DARKNET.LNK both show up consistently across all three surfaces after the relevant state change

items.spec:
Wire the already-defined but currently unused .kp-dghost/.kp-dghost-arm/.kp-dghost-node classes (styles.css ~1766-1780, CSS already ties opacity to :hover) into DuelCellView (duel-board.tsx). For every cell in the `legal` set while a piece is ARMED-FOR-PLACEMENT, render a <g className="kp-dghost"> containing armLines(armedPiece.mask, 'kp-dghost-arm', 5) plus a small kp-dghost-node circle, using the piece's FIXED mask exactly as held (never rotated to fit; the whole point of a shaped piece is that orientation is not yours to choose). No new CSS is required for the legal case: the existing :hover opacity rule does the fade-in. Insert this <g> BEFORE (earlier in DOM order than, i.e. painted under) the existing kp-daim aim-bracket <g> within the same cell group, so if a future ability ever makes a block cell also an aim target, the machine's telegraph brackets still paint on top. In practice this never fires today: aim brackets only ever attach to kind==='node' cells and ghost previews only ever attach to kind==='block' cells (per the existing 'Blocks are only ever legal while a patch cell is being aimed' comment in duel-board.tsx:79-80), so the two are mutually exclusive by cell kind, not just by DOM order.

HOVER-ILLEGAL: while a piece is armed, slag blocks that exist but are out of reach currently get no feedback at all (no legal class, no cursor, no onClick). Add one small class, applied to block cells that are in-range-of-nothing while placing is active: .kp-dblock-oor { cursor: not-allowed; } and .kp-dblock-oor .kp-dblock-body { stroke: var(--kp-crimson); stroke-opacity: 0.55; }. This is a static tint, not a pulse (the pulse is reserved for legal targets, per kp-dblock-patchable), so legal and illegal never compete for attention.

TOUCH FALLBACK: touch has no hover, so the existing kp-targetbar text ('PATCH CELL: pick a slag block within reach (1 RAM)', duel.tsx ~638-649) gains a small inline PieceGlyph at 20px (see patch-pouch-strip) directly before the text, showing the armed piece's shape to every player, not just mouse users, and giving touch players the shape information hover would otherwise carry.
acceptance: the ghost overlay renders the exact fixed mask of the armed piece, never a rotated or generic cross regardless of which of the 4 shapes is armed
on every legal slag cell, hovering shows the ghost at 0.85 opacity via the existing :hover rule; leaving hover returns it to 0
out-of-reach slag blocks show a static crimson-tinted outline and a not-allowed cursor while a piece is armed, with no animation competing against the legal-target pulse

the ghost <g> is never the last-painted element in a cell group that also renders kp-daim; automated or manual DOM-order check confirms aim brackets, on the rare cell that could carry both, always paint last
the target bar shows the armed piece's shape as a glyph, not just text, so a touch player who cannot hover still knows what they are about to place before they tap a target

items.spec:
Lives entirely in the KitScreen kit card (kp-kit-cells, see patch-pouch-strip surface 3), available whenever LOADOUT.CFG is open and there is no active dive (never inside duel.tsx; the dock only supports SELECT and PLACE, not fuse). Uses the existing but unwired .kp-piece-actions button stack (styles.css ~1588-1611, already styled at 8px caps with a disabled state at opacity .4) as each piece slot's action row, with a single button: CRAFT.

STATE no-pair-legal: clicking a held piece's CRAFT button (or the glyph itself) selects it as piece A (gold outline, same .kp-ability-arming treatment as the dock's armed state). The engine checks every other held piece for a strictly-larger arm union (legal only when the union has more arms set than either input alone, i.e. it is not just a duplicate or a subset). If none exist, every other slot dims to a 'no partner' state (reuse .kp-mode-locked's opacity 0.35) and a status line under the card header reads 'NO PARTNER: every combination repeats an arm you already have.' (placeholder). Clicking A again, or a CANCEL affordance next to the status line, clears the selection.

STATE pair-armed: pieces that DO form a legal union get a highlight distinct from 'no partner': reuse the .kp-dlegal-ring dashed gold pulse styling (already used on the board for legal rotation targets) applied to their .kp-piece-slot border instead of dimming them. Hovering (mouse) or tapping (any input) a legal partner arms it as piece B and shows a live RESULT PREVIEW: a third glyph slot at the card's top, 56px, using the .kp-pp-hi highlighted-stroke variant already defined, rendering the OR of the two masks with its shape name resolved (STRAIGHT/ELBOW/TEE/CROSS placeholder). A FUSE button appears next to the preview (never auto-commits on tap or hover-out, mirroring the duel's own pick-then-'CAST NOW' pattern so a destructive two-item spend is never accidental). A CANCEL button next to it clears back to no selection with zero side effects, whether zero, one, or two pieces are currently selected.

STATE crafted: on FUSE, the two input glyphs play the existing .kp-claimpop / kp-claim-in pop-out (240ms, steps(4), scale 1.35 to 0.92 to 1, already defined for board claims) and are removed from their slots; the union glyph pops into the freed slot with the same animation; a small gold caps stamp 'PIECE FUSED' (placeholder, reuse .kp-draft-stamp positioning/typography) shows for about 600ms then fades. Fires the new pieceFuse sfx (see sfx item) at the moment the union glyph appears, preceded by two short existing claimTick pulses (~90ms and ~45ms before the hit, rate 0.85 and 0.95, vol 0.5) representing the two inputs converging, the same compositional idiom playCascade already uses for multi-hit sequences.
acceptance: selecting piece A always produces exactly one of two states: every other held piece shown as a legal partner (gold dashed pulse) or, if none exist, every other piece shown dimmed with the no-partner status line; there is no state where a piece is neither highlighted nor dimmed

the result preview glyph always matches the true bitwise OR of the two selected masks; if the game later allows a union to resolve into a shape rarer than what a legal-partner check should have permitted, that is treated as an engine bug this UI must never mask by clamping or approximating the preview
FUSE is never triggered by hover alone; a player must take an explicit confirming action after both pieces are selected
CANCEL at any point (zero, one, or two pieces picked) returns to the pre-selection pouch state with no pieces removed and no credits or state changed
the crafted result glyph's pop-in animation and the PIECE FUSED stamp both complete within 1 second so repeated crafting is never rate-limited by its own animation

items.when: the instant a two-piece craft resolves into its union glyph (patch-craft-flow's 'crafted' state). Deliberately distinct from the existing 'granted' preset (square wave, clean arpeggio, used for augment picks and old patch-cell buys): pieceFuse is a sawtooth with a phaser sweep, reading as a mechanical weld rather than a reward chime, so the two sounds are never confused even played back to back. Preceded by two short existing 'claimTick' hits (see patch-craft-flow spec) representing the two inputs converging; those need no new preset.

items.spec: New floating window, chrome identical to the existing MANUAL.TXT/LEDGER.LOG utility windows (kp-fw shell from wm.tsx, toggled by wm.toggle('darknet') from a new desktop icon, not part of the UNCLOSABLE_SCREENS 'flow' window). Add a WinDef entry to shop-os.tsx's WIN_DEFS: { id: 'darknet', title: 'DARKNET.LNK', x: 420, y: 150, w: 400 }. Add a 6th DesktopIcon to the IconGrid, always visible regardless of night/day state (per the 'teach by showing, not hiding' pattern already used for locked ATTACK/DEFEND modes showing a '?' rather than disappearing): the player should see DARKNET.LNK exists long before they can use it. DESKTOP ICON: this is the one deliberate exception to the desktop's all-inline-SVG-rect icon idiom (see the filed art order icon-darknet). Every other DesktopIcon (JobsIcon, LoadoutIcon, ManualIcon, LedgerIcon) is hand-built from on a 32x32 grid using currentColor, so it recolors on hover/focus for free. DARKNET.LNK instead renders the ordered pixel-art PNG as a plain (image-rendering: pixelated already applies globally). The visual 'wrongness' of a raster icon sitting among vector ones is the point: this is a bootleg tool the player installed, not native KP/OS chrome, and it should look like it does not quite belong. Add 'darknet' to the IconName union and ICONS record with a small DarknetIcon() wrapper returning that . If the art order is not ready when this ships, fall back to a hand-drawn SVG glyph in the native idiom (a simple padlock-over-circuit silhouette) so the feature is never blocked on art; swap to the ordered PNG when it lands. OFFLINE STATE (run.screen !== 'upgrade', i.e. any time other than the night/day-close phase): window still opens and is fully readable, but shows a static muted panel: kp-rail-dim text reading 'OFFLINE. The signal only answers after close.' (placeholder), no BUY control rendered at all (not just disabled; a control that can never fire in this state should not exist in this state, matching how the duel dock never renders a program button for a mode the player has not unlocked). A single low-opacity (about 0.12) piece-shape watermark using the desktop icon art sits behind the text purely as texture. VENDOR STATE (run.screen === 'upgrade'): a single row, styled exactly like the existing .kp-patchrow pattern (ghost button plus an adjacent .kp-rail-dim span in the SAME flex row), reading '{credits} cr on hand - pouch {n}/5' (placeholder copy). This is the credit-adjacency rule from tutorial/ledger.md's night-shop-credit-adjacency fix applied on day one for this new spend surface, not retrofitted later: price and balance always share a row. BUY is disabled, with a title attribute explaining why, whenever credits < price or the pouch is at 5/5 (mirrors the existing buyPatchCell disabled/title pattern in UpgradeScreen). THE REVEAL BEAT (the sfx/animation centerpiece of this pass): clicking BUY deducts credits immediately (matching every other buy in the game, no extra confirm step) and the engine rolls the shape at that instant. The UI then plays a reel: a single glyph slot cycles through a sequence of decoy shapes with a hard, un-tweened content swap on every tick (no cross-fade; this game's whole animation idiom is steps(), never interpolation, and a slot reel is the most literal expression of that available). Schedule: 7 ticks at [70, 70, 80, 90, 105, 120, 140]ms intervals (about 675ms total), each accompanied by the existing 'tick' preset (bus ui, rate climbing from about 0.9 to 1.2, jitter 0.02, vol 0.3), landing on the true rolled shape on the final tick. On lock: the glyph plays the existing kp-claimpop pop-in (240ms steps(4)), a gold/signal glow flashes around it, the caption reveals the shape name in caps, and the new darknetReveal sting (see sfx item) fires at this exact frame, never at the initial BUY click. Hold the locked state about 600ms, then the row returns to buyable (or to its disabled state if the pouch is now full or credits ran out). Total beat: under 1.6 seconds. Under prefers-reduced-motion, skip straight to the locked glyph with no cycling; the sting still fires at that mount, since it is the payoff sound, not a byproduct of the animation.
acceptance: the window opens from its own desktop icon and behaves like MANUAL.TXT/LEDGER.LOG: draggable, closable, independent of the flow window's screen
outside the night phase the window shows OFFLINE with no BUY control anywhere in the DOM, not merely a disabled one
during the night phase, price and the player's current credit balance always render inside the same row/flex container as the BUY action, at every reachable state of that row
BUY is disabled with an explanatory title whenever credits are short or the pouch already holds 5, exactly mirroring the existing buyPatchCell disabled/title convention
the reel always lands on the shape the engine actually rolled; there is never a frame where the locked glyph disagrees with the piece added to the pouch
the darknetReveal sting fires exactly once per purchase, at the visual lock, never at the BUY click and never twice
the full reveal beat, click to buyable-again, completes in under 1.6 seconds so a player buying several pieces in a row across nights is never made to wait
under prefers-reduced-motion the reel does not cycle, but the sting still plays and the shape is still legible before the row resets

items.when: the exact frame the DARKNET.LNK reel locks onto the rolled piece shape, preceded by 7 existing 'tick' presets on a decelerating schedule (see darknet-window spec). No other payoff sound in the palette (granted, unlock, stamp) uses a phaser sweep; it is reserved for this one moment so a player learns to associate that specific texture with the darknet reveal and nothing else, the first time they hear it.

items.spec:
Redesigns the existing kp-cleanrun block (screens.tsx ~467-476) into a piece-aware reveal, since a dropped piece IS the clean-run reward under the new system (per the brief's 'reworked CLEAN RUN'). If the economy also grants a piece through some other independent per-job roll, this same component and both its states apply there too; the visual design here is agnostic to how many trigger paths feed it, keyed off whatever result field the reducer exposes (currently r.cleanRun; likely becomes something like r.pieceDrop: { shape, capped } | null).

Rename the block kp-cleanrun to kp-piecedrop (same gold-border, gold-tinted-background chrome, styles.css ~1146-1170, no structural change needed there) and give it two states, both showing the actual glyph rather than only text, since seeing the shape is the entire point of a piece reveal:

BANKED: a 44px PieceGlyph (see patch-pouch-strip) at signal tone, the shape name in caps, and a gold 'PIECE BANKED' stamp (placeholder, reuse .kp-draft-stamp corner typography).

CAPPED: pouch already at 5/5. Same glyph but rendered dim/crossed using the existing .kp-chip-capped muted-gold convention (already established for the strain chip's 40-cap case, styles.css ~1209-1212), text stating the pouch is full and, if the reducer supplies a salvage credit value (mirroring the existing dry-augment-cache salvage row directly above it in kp-chip-breakdown), showing that number the same way ('+{salvage} cr' in em). If no salvage value is supplied, the row simply states the piece was lost to a full pouch with no credit line, rather than inventing a number.

Placement: directly after the existing kp-cleanrun/kp-piecedrop position (payout, then strain chip breakdown, then this), before the augment draft section, so the read order stays payout, cost, physical loot, then the headline decision (augment draft).

Sound: on mount, if a piece drop is present, fire the existing 'patchPlace' preset (bus ui, vol 0.6) for BANKED at a slight delay (about 150ms) so it never stacks exactly on top of the existing draft 'unlock' cue at 300ms when both fire on the same result. For CAPPED, fire the existing 'tick' preset (bus ui, low vol) instead: understated, since the player still received value (salvage or otherwise), not a denial.
acceptance: the BANKED and CAPPED states are visually distinguishable at a glance (color/opacity of the glyph, not just the caption text)
the glyph shown always matches the actual shape added to (or, if capped, offered to and rejected by) the pouch
the capped row never shows a salvage number the reducer did not supply
when both a piece drop and an augment draft appear on the same result, their mount sounds are audibly staggered, not simultaneous
this block's position never sits between the strain breakdown and the augment draft's heading in a way that separates the chip math from its own total

items.spec: Three surfaces, one shared concept: boosts are capped at a bay count (base 3, purchasable to 5 for 150cr then 300cr per the brief); config augments are explicitly exempt from the cap. SURFACE 1, KitScreen bay card (screens.tsx ~337-357). Split the existing combined kp-kit-augs card into two cards, which makes the cap-exemption self-evident without a coachmark (a tier-0 contribution: coordinate with tutorial-agent's boostSlots mechanic entry, this may retire the need for a moment on that specific fact). New kp-kit-card kp-kit-bays: header 'BOOST BAYS' with '{filled}/{bayCount}' in the em slot exactly like every other kit card header; a pip row directly below reusing the existing .kp-pip/.kp-pip-on convention (already used for RAM) at bayCount total pips, filled = installed boost count; then the existing .kp-aug-list styling below, filtered to kind==='boost' only. The remaining original card keeps its 'AUGMENTS' header but is now CONFIGS-only (kind==='config'), with a line under the header stating configs do not count against the bay cap (placeholder copy). SURFACE 2, UpgradeScreen INSTALL BOOST BAY row (screens.tsx, in the retired kp-cellrow's old slot, since deterministic patch-cell buying moves to DARKNET.LNK). Same .kp-patchrow structure as every other night-shop row: 'BOOST BAYS {bayCount}/5 - {credits} cr' in one row (credit-adjacency again). At 5/5 the button reads 'BOOST BAYS MAXED (5)' and disables, mirroring the existing RAM/tier maxed-button convention already in this screen (run.ramPerTurn >= MAX_RAM). Cost reads 150 for the 4th bay, 300 for the 5th, straight from the brief's numbers. SURFACE 3, ResultScreen pick-to-swap (screens.tsx ~479-516, the existing augment draft). Step 1 is entirely unchanged: pick a card from r.draft as today. Step 2 is new and only triggers when the picked card's kind is 'boost' AND the player's installed boost count already equals bayCount at the moment of picking. Instead of instant-install, the draft grid is replaced by an EJECT sub-view: the just-picked boost pinned at the top with an 'INCOMING' tag (reuse .kp-draft-picked gold treatment) and, below it, the player's owned boost augments rendered as selectable buttons in the existing .kp-aug-list style. Tapping one arms it as the eject target (gold outline, same .kp-ability-arming idiom used everywhere else an item is armed-not-committed in this game); a confirming EJECT button appears once a target is armed (never auto-commits on tap alone, matching patch-craft-flow's FUSE and the duel's CAST NOW pattern for every destructive two-step action in this game). A CANCEL button is present from the moment the sub-view opens and at every point after: it discards the just-picked boost entirely, ejects nothing, and returns to the original draft grid so the player may pick a different card, or take the existing SKIP THE DRAFT action. On EJECT: the removed augment's list row shows an 'EJECTED' stamp (reuse .kp-draft-stamp corner typography, about 500ms) using the same transient setTimeout-plus-state pattern UpgradeScreen already uses for its regen-pop reveal (screens.tsx ~548-557), then the row is removed from the list; the newly picked boost gets the existing 'INSTALLED' picked-card treatment. Config picks never trigger this sub-view, at any bay fill level, since configs are exempt from the cap by design.
acceptance: the CONFIGS card and the new BOOST BAYS card are visibly separate on KitScreen, with the bay card's pip row always reading filled/bayCount accurately against the actual installed boost count
the UpgradeScreen install row and its credits-adjacent span always share one flex row, at every state (buyable, maxed, insufficient credits)
picking a boost when under bay capacity installs exactly as it does today, with no swap step ever appearing
picking a boost when at bay capacity always shows the eject sub-view before anything is removed or installed
CANCEL at any point in the eject sub-view leaves the player's kit, credits, and bay contents byte-identical to before the pick
EJECT always removes exactly the armed target and installs exactly the incoming boost, never any other pairing
a picked config augment never triggers the eject sub-view regardless of current boost fill
